open_points.subject: A17 configuration-file path resolution
open_points.text: a relative one from the working directory
open_points.question: For configuration re-reads before later requests, does a relative command-line path remain anchored to the working directory captured at startup, or is it resolved from the process's working directory at each re-read?
options: Capture and retain a descriptor for the startup working directory
Resolve from the current working directory on every read
Convert the path to an absolute path at startup
open_points.default_guess: Capture the startup working-directory descriptor and use it for every read.

open_points.subject: A18 data-directory initialization
open_points.text: The data directory holds one SQLite database with every kernel record, a content-addressed area of value bytes and file fixtures named by digest, and the run spool, one subdirectory per run.
open_points.question: What happens when the data directory, database, value area, fixture area, spool area, or lock object does not yet exist, and which of them may the kernel create?
options: Create every missing store artifact securely
Require the data directory to exist but create its internal artifacts
Refuse startup if any artifact is missing
open_points.default_guess: Require a pre-existing private data directory and securely create missing internal store artifacts.

open_points.subject: A18 data-directory root path
open_points.text: Every file of the directory is opened without following symbolic links; a link found at start stops the start
open_points.question: Does the no-symlink rule also cover the configured data-directory path itself and every ancestor component, or only entries beneath the resolved data directory?
options: Reject symlinks in the data-directory path and all descendants
Reject only the data-directory entry itself and descendants
Allow the configured path to resolve through symlinks but reject links inside it
open_points.default_guess: Reject symlinks in the data-directory path and in every descendant opened by the store.

open_points.subject: A18 store layout validation
open_points.text: The data directory holds one SQLite database with every kernel record, a content-addressed area of value bytes and file fixtures named by digest, and the run spool, one subdirectory per run.
open_points.question: Must startup refuse unknown entries or unexpected file types such as devices, FIFOs and sockets, or may unrelated private entries remain in the data directory?
options: Refuse every unrecognized entry and every unexpected file type
Allow unknown regular files but refuse special files
Ignore all unknown entries except symbolic links
open_points.default_guess: Refuse unexpected file types but leave unknown private regular files untouched.

open_points.subject: A18 private store permissions
open_points.text: The directory and everything in it are private to the kernel's user; the kernel refuses to start otherwise.
open_points.question: What exact ownership and permission conditions constitute “private,” including directory execute bits, group/other bits, ACLs, and files the kernel creates?
options: Require ownership by the effective kernel user and no group/other permission bits
Also reject ACLs that grant access to another principal
Rely only on the data directory's permissions and do not inspect every child
open_points.default_guess: Require the effective kernel user to own every entry, reject all group/other permission bits, and create new entries with owner-only modes.

open_points.subject: A18 permission changes after startup
open_points.text: The directory and everything in it are private to the kernel's user; the kernel refuses to start otherwise.
open_points.question: If ownership or permissions become non-private after startup, must each affected store call detect and refuse them, must the kernel stop, or are permissions checked only at startup?
options: Recheck safely on every open and fail only the affected store call
Recheck and stop the kernel on any change
Check only at startup and trust the host afterward
open_points.default_guess: Recheck the entry on every open and fail the affected store call with nothing written.

open_points.subject: A18 exclusive store lock
open_points.text: At start it takes an exclusive lock in the data directory; a second process on the same directory refuses to start.
open_points.question: What object and Linux locking primitive define the exclusive lock, when is it acquired and released, and must its descriptor be prevented from being inherited by child processes?
options: Hold a non-inherited flock lock on a fixed regular lock file for the process lifetime
Hold a non-inherited fcntl record lock on the SQLite database
Use an atomically created sentinel file with explicit stale-lock recovery
open_points.default_guess: Hold a close-on-exec flock lock on a fixed owner-only regular file for the kernel process's lifetime.

open_points.subject: A18 startup refusal precedence
open_points.text: At start it takes an exclusive lock in the data directory; a second process on the same directory refuses to start. The directory and everything in it are private to the kernel's user; the kernel refuses to start otherwise. Every file of the directory is opened without following symbolic links; a link found at start stops the start
open_points.question: What is the exact order of the lock, data-directory ownership and mode checks, symlink scan, database validation, cleanup, A17 configuration checks, and A03 sandbox probe when several startup conditions fail?
options: Use decision and rule order across A17, A18, A03 and A20
Define one explicit global startup-check sequence
Startup may report any encountered failure
open_points.default_guess: Define and use one explicit global startup-check sequence before opening the surface.

open_points.subject: A18 request serialization
open_points.text: Surface requests are handled one at a time in the order they arrive
open_points.question: What event establishes arrival order when requests reach the MCP surface concurrently?
options: Order when a complete request message is received
Order when authentication begins
Order by a monotonic sequence assigned on connection acceptance
Permit either concurrent request to be first
open_points.default_guess: Assign a store-independent sequence when each complete request message is received and process by that sequence.

open_points.subject: A18 file and record crash durability
open_points.text: Value bytes and spooled files are written to a temporary file, flushed, checked against their digest and size, and then renamed into place; a completed file a record names is never overwritten
open_points.question: Which objects must be durably flushed, and in what order relative to rename and SQLite commit, so a crash or power loss cannot leave a committed record naming a missing or incomplete file?
options: Flush the temporary file, rename it, flush the containing directory, then commit and durably flush SQLite
Treat rename completion as sufficient and then commit SQLite
Guarantee only process-crash safety, not power-loss durability
open_points.default_guess: Flush the file, rename it, flush its directory, and only then commit the SQLite transaction with full durability.

open_points.subject: A18 startup cleanup failures
open_points.text: On start, temporary files, value bytes no record names ... and the spool directories of runs that ended and do not keep their spool ... are removed; nothing else is. A spool directory that cannot be removed does not stop the start
open_points.question: Does the same continue-start rule apply when a temporary file or unreferenced value byte file cannot be removed, or must that failure stop startup?
options: Continue startup for every cleanup failure and never serve the leftovers
Continue only for ended-run spool cleanup; refuse startup for temporary or unreferenced value cleanup failure
Refuse startup for any cleanup failure
open_points.default_guess: Continue startup for all cleanup failures while ensuring no leftover unreferenced file can be served.

open_points.subject: A18 database failure handling
open_points.text: The data directory holds one SQLite database with every kernel record
open_points.question: What must startup do when the database is unreadable, malformed, corrupt, has an unsupported schema, or cannot provide the required transaction and durability behavior?
options: Refuse startup and identify the store check that failed
Create or repair the database automatically
Start with a new empty database
Leave the outcome as an internal error
open_points.default_guess: Refuse startup without modifying or replacing the database.
